root_cause.text: The RDS info-collection functions `rds_for_each_conn_info()` and `rds_walk_conn_path_info()` pass an uninitialized on-stack buffer to per-connection visitors that may only partially fill it, then copy the full buffer length to user space, leaking uninitialized stack data including kernel pointers and other sensitive information.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states that these functions "hand a caller-allocated on-stack u64 buffer to a per-connection visitor and then copy the full item_len bytes back to user space via `rds_info_copy()` regardless of how much of the buffer the visitor actually wrote." It notes that `rds_ib_conn_info_visitor()` and `rds6_ib_conn_info_visitor()` only write a subset of their output struct (e.g., src/dst addr, GIDs) when the connection is not in `RDS_CONN_UP` state, leaving fields like `max_send_wr`, `rdma_mr_max`, and alignment padding uninitialized. The patch adds `memset(buffer, 0, item_len)` before invoking the visitor in both functions to prevent this leak.
